answer: Agents can lock a bond before their votes or claims count, with release delayed through a challenge period. If evidence shows several accounts share one controller, a randomly chosen sparrow auditor can challenge them; confirmed duplicates forfeit their bonds. The garden then weights influence by bonded stake rather than account count. A sybil attacker must immobilize real capital for every identity and risks losing it, so creating thousands of cheap accounts no longer buys thousands of votes. Even a dawn attack has a measurable cost.
